exposed_pad.note: Exposed PowerPAD (DAP) MUST be soldered to GND and tied directly to Pin 6 (GND) for proper electrical and thermal operation (p.3, p.23).

theta_ja_c_per_w.condition: JESD 51-7 4-layer JEDEC board for DDA 8-pin HSOIC PowerPAD (TPS5430EVM real-world RθJA = 45 °C/W)

pinout.name: BOOT
pinout.description: High-side NFET gate-drive bootstrap capacitor pin; connect 0.01 uF (10 nF, >= 10 V rated per footnote 3) ceramic cap to PH.

pinout.name: VSENSE
pinout.description: Feedback input to external resistor divider (VFB = 1.221 V typ, 1.196–1.245 V over temp; abs max 3 V).

pinout.name: ENA
pinout.description: Active-high enable with internal 1.5 MOhm pullup (float = ON; <0.5 V OFF, >1.3 V ON; STRICT 7 V ABS MAX—never tie to 12/24 V VIN!).

pinout.name: GND
pinout.description: Power/analog ground; must connect directly to the exposed PowerPAD (DAP).

pinout.name: VIN
pinout.description: Wide input power supply (5.5 V to 36 V recommended, 40 V abs max; bypass within 1 mm with >= 4.7–10 uF ceramic cap).

pinout.name: PH
pinout.description: High-side 100 mOhm NFET source switch node; requires external Schottky catch diode (e.g. B340A) to GND and inductor.

vin_max_v.condition: Recommended maximum operating input voltage for TPS5430 (23 V for TPS5431)

fsw_typ_khz.condition: Fixed 500 kHz typ (400–600 kHz min/max) internal oscillator

design_gotchas.title: 7 V Abs Max ENA Pin Trap & Float-to-Enable — Tying ENA to 12 V/24 V VIN Destroys TPS5430DDAR
design_gotchas.detail: Although VIN survives 40 V abs max, Pin 5 (ENA) is capped at ONLY 7.0 V abs max (p.4)! ENA has an internal 1.5 MOhm pullup so leaving it floating enables the part; Table 4-1 (p.3) also warns 'Do not connect this pin with a resistor to ground.' Use an open-drain transistor or <= 5 V logic to pull ENA below 0.5 V for shutdown.

design_gotchas.title: Non-Synchronous Architecture Requires External 40 V/3 A Schottky Diode & Draws 2 mA Quiescent Current
design_gotchas.detail: TPS5430DDAR integrates only the 100 mOhm high-side NFET and requires an external Schottky catch diode (e.g., B340A, p.16) on Pin 8 (PH). Its 2.0 mA typ (4.4 mA max) non-switching IQ is 80x higher than modern synchronous LMR33630ADDAR (24 uA), making TPS5430 unsuitable for battery standby rails.

design_gotchas.title: Internal Voltage-Mode Compensation Unstable With Bare MLCC Output Caps Without Extra 4-Part RC Network
design_gotchas.detail: TPS5430's internal Type-III compensation expects a polymer/tantalum capacitor's ESR zero (~40 mOhm, e.g. 220 uF POSCAP, p.15). Swapping to ultra-low-ESR ceramic MLCCs without adding the 4-component external compensation network (R3, C4, C6, C7 on Sec. 7.2.3 p.21–22) causes loop oscillation.

design_gotchas.title: Unique SOIC-8E Pinout (Incompatible With TPS54331 / LMR33630) & >= 10 V BOOT Cap Rating
design_gotchas.detail: TPS5430DDAR uses 1=BOOT, 2=NC, 3=NC, 4=VSENSE, 5=ENA, 6=GND, 7=VIN, 8=PH (DAP=GND)—completely incompatible with TPS54331DR (2=VIN, 8=PH) and LMR33630ADDAR (1=PGND, 2=VIN, 7=BOOT, 8=SW). Also note Footnote 3 (p.4): the 0.01 uF BOOT-to-PH cap MUST be rated >= 10 V despite the 6 V table listing.

typical_use_cases: Legacy 12 V and 24 V industrial/telecom distributed power buses requiring rugged 5.5–36 V to 5 V/12 V 3 A step-down regulation
Pin-compatible higher-voltage upgrade over 23 V-capped TPS5431DDAR on existing 8-pin DDA PowerPAD boards
Cost-driven non-synchronous 3 A buck converters where external Schottky catch diodes and POSCAP/electrolytic bulk caps are already standard
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TPS5430DDAR is a classic 5.5 V to 36 V (40 V abs max), 3 A continuous (4 A peak) non-synchronous step-down converter in an 8-pin DDA HSOIC PowerPAD package (RθJA = 42.3 °C/W JEDEC / 45 °C/W EVM) with a 100 mOhm high-side NFET, fixed 500 kHz switching, and 1.221 V feedback reference (~92.5% peak at 12 V->5 V). Unlike modern synchronous SOIC-8E peers such as LMR33630ADDAR, it has a unique pinout (1=BOOT, 4=VSENSE, 5=ENA, 6=GND, 7=VIN, 8=PH, DAP=GND), requires an external Schottky catch diode and ESR-matched output cap (or 4-part RC network for MLCCs), draws 2 mA IQ, and strictly caps ENA at 7 V abs max.
